title: Who votes no, and on what
question: What share of each supervisor’s and each commissioner’s land-use votes are no votes, and which kinds of matter draw them?
finding: Supervisors cast 20,840 aye or no votes on land-use matters at the Board and its committees from 2015 to 2026 and 232 (1.1%) were no votes, from 0.0% (Alan Wong, 284 votes) to 6.1% (John Avalos, 198). Planning Commissioners voted no in 3.2% of 9,716 votes in the 2019-2022 minutes, from 0.9% (Diamond) to 8.3% (Ruiz).
how: Every aye and no in the Board’s roll calls on the 1,872 land-use files (full Board and committees), with one vote printed on several sibling appeal files counted once; and every aye and no printed in Planning Commission and Historic Preservation Commission minutes (January 2019 to August 2022, with 1 earlier hearing in April 2018). “Sole no” counts votes where the member was the only dissenter. “Most often against” lists the kinds of matter of the member’s no votes. Members with fewer than 20 votes are left out. Commissioners appear by surname because the minutes print surnames only.
limits: A no vote is not a vote against a project: on an appeal, voting no on the motion to affirm is a vote for the appellant, and many roll calls are votes to postpone or amend. Members served in different years with different business before them, and committee members vote on items before they are settled. A low share of no votes can also reflect agreement reached before the vote. The commission minutes cover only 2019-2022. A difference between areas, or between groups of cases, is not proof of bias. Areas differ in what is proposed, in zoning, lot sizes, building ages and land prices, and in who chooses to apply, object or appeal at all.
